_meta.indication: Treatment of adult patients with unresectable or metastatic, HR-positive, HER2-negative (IHC 0, IHC 1+ or IHC 2+/ISH-) breast cancer who have received prior endocrine-based therapy and chemotherapy for unresectable or metastatic disease

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, open-label, randomized trial; patients randomized 1:1 to DATROWAY 6 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks or investigator's choice of chemotherapy
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with unresectable or metastatic HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer who progressed on and were not suitable for further endocrine therapy and had received 1 or 2 prior lines of chemotherapy in the metastatic setting; ECOG PS 0 or 1
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Major efficacy outcomes were progression-free survival (PFS) by BICR per RECIST v1.1 and overall survival (OS)
pivotal_trials.result: Median PFS 6.9 vs 4.9 months; HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.52, 0.76); p<0.0001. OS not improved: median 18.6 vs 18.3 months, HR 1.01 (95% CI 0.83, 1.22), NS. Confirmed ORR 36% vs 23%.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥10%): stomatitis (59%), nausea (56%), fatigue (44%), alopecia (38%), constipation (34%), dry eye (27%), keratitis (24%), vomiting (24%). Warnings: ILD/pneumonitis (4.2%, 0.3% fatal), ocular adverse reactions (51%), and stomatitis (59%).
target_moa: Trop-2-directed antibody-drug conjugate; a humanized anti-Trop2 IgG1 mAb conjugated to DXd, a topoisomerase I inhibitor, via a cleavable linker. After binding Trop2 and internalization, released DXd causes DNA damage and apoptotic cell death.

rems.type: REMS not required; safety issues managed through labeling and routine post-marketing surveillance

companion_dx_detail: No application for a device or companion diagnostic was submitted or planned with this BLA

advisory_committee.vote: FDA did not refer this application to an advisory committee as there were no efficacy or safety issues requiring external input

basis.text: Standard review, not priority review, was granted to this application

summary.text: Standard-review BLA approved on the basis of the randomized TROPION-Breast01 trial showing a statistically significant PFS improvement; no accelerated approval, breakthrough, fast track, orphan, or priority-review designations; no REMS required and no companion diagnostic; not referred to an advisory committee.

citations.quote: The FDA notes that standard review, not priority review, was granted to this application.
The study demonstrated a statistically significant improvement in PFS in patients randomized to DATROWAY compared to chemotherapy.
The review team determined that a REMS is not required for this application.

requirement.text: 4776-1 Conduct an integrated analysis of data from clinical trials and observational studies (e.g., real world evidence), post-marketing reports, and other sources to further characterize the safety and efficacy/effectiveness of datopotamab deruxtecan in patients of underrepresented racial and ethnic minority groups with unresectable or metastatic HR+HER2- breast cancer (especially Black patients given their underrepresentation in the TROPION-Breast01 trial).

This should also include pharmacokinetic data, if available.
